s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory and cardiac symptoms with signs of inflammation and a mass in the mediastinum
salient_findings: Muffled heart sounds and decreased breath sounds at the right lower zone
Mediastinal widening on chest radiograph and large pericardial effusion on echocardiography
key_facts: 1-week history of dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain
Worse symptoms when supine
Associated with orthopnea, mild agitation, and fever
Intermittent fever over the preceding 3 months
No significant past medical history
No known contact with COVID-19 patients
Febrile, alert, and in mild respiratory distress on examination
Decreased breath sounds at the right lower zone on lung auscultation
Muffled heart sounds on cardiac examination
Hepatomegaly on abdominal examination
Mediastinal widening on chest radiograph
Sinus tachycardia with low-voltage QRS and electrical alternans on ECG
Large pericardial effusion on transthoracic echocardiography
Anterior mediastinal mass with moderate pleural and pericardial effusions on contrast-enhanced thoracic CT

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and symptoms consistent with lymphoma

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss

shortlist.label: Thymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Anterior mediastinal mass and pericardial effusion

shortlist.label: Castleman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and systemic inflammatory symptoms

shortlist.label: Lymphoblastic lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and symptoms consistent with aggressive lymphoma

raw.rationale: The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass, large pericardial effusion, and pleural effusions, along with systemic symptoms such as fever and hepatomegaly, are highly suggestive of lymphoblastic lymphoma, which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that often presents with a mediastinal mass and can cause pericardial and pleural effusions.

rejected.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: While Hodgkin lymphoma can also present with a mediastinal mass, the presence of a large pericardial effusion and pleural effusions, along with the patient's age and symptoms, make lymphoblastic lymphoma a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broad category that includes lymphoblastic lymphoma, but is too general to be the champion diagnosis.

rejected.label: Thymoma
rejected.why: Thymoma can present with a mediastinal mass, but it is less likely to cause large pericardial and pleural effusions, and is more commonly seen in older adults.

rejected.label: Castleman disease
rejected.why: Castleman disease can present with systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy, but it is less likely to cause a large anterior mediastinal mass and pericardial and pleural effusions.
